evidence.fact: Tattletale’s mostly empty “End of the World” board tracks Jack’s route, recruitment and killings after he left Brockton Bay. A note records limits to Dinah’s forecasts: less accurate at interactions with power-immune capes, precogs or situational-change Thinkers, and limited visibility beyond such “stoppers”; it lists several towns without known stoppers and Boston/Charlestown with some but no known direct Nine interaction. Taylor understands the board as using forecast blind spots to narrow Jack’s possible location.
evidence.limits: The board contains little beyond Jack’s trail and a single Dinah-limits card; Taylor’s interpretation is a reconstruction, and the Boston/Charlestown note calls for double-checking with “Still.” It does not establish Jack’s current location.
evidence.knowledge: Taylor reads Lisa’s private notes; she has not independently verified each town’s status or the completeness of the route.
evidence.review: Parent inspected complete original claim object; coverage binds exact reader notes and prior review receipt. W227 initial worker21.5 heading corrected to manifest Imago21.7.

An attempted intruder is shocked; local law enforcement reprimands him for excessive lethal security. He abandons town and learns to sell in distributed larger markets.

evidence.fact: Fei accidentally moves a rock on a gentle slope and reveals a new spring stronger than A; Ma actually renames him Fei Hong Yun. Seven days later Hei surrounds the valley, and Gu pollution blackens all three springs overnight. Ma proposes giving outsiders the Ma surname to prevent wholesale absorption.
evidence.limits: Fei Hong Yun is the performed new name; Ma Hong Yun is not yet granted. Ancestor blessing and feared outsider bans are Ma’s interpretations. The surname plan is still proposed, not implemented, and neither cure nor pollution caster/mechanism is identified.
